classification.difficultyReason: Check intentional inconsistencies against the appropriate angle relationship and justify each judgement.

content.prompt: Decide whether these diagrams have the correct information or not. Justify your answer.

spec.description: Vertical and horizontal arms form a marked right angle, subdivided by an upward-right arm. Labels 60° and 25° occupy the upper and lower sectors. Plain endpoints; no fill.
spec.mathematics: The square requires 90°, but the two printed subdivisions total 85°. Preserve this intentional inconsistency.
spec.answerVisibility: All arms, the right-angle marker and both angle givens are student-visible. The completed blue response is answer-only.

answer.short: No. $60^\circ+25^\circ=85^\circ$, but angles in a right angle must sum to $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$60^\circ+25^\circ=85^\circ$$
No. Angles in a right angle must sum to $90^\circ$, and $85^\circ\ne90^\circ$.

spec.description: Named arms CA and CB open left, with A above-left and B below-left. A square marks the minor angle; an undirected reflex arc runs around the right side and is labelled 260°. C is immediately right of the vertex.
spec.mathematics: The marked 90° minor angle and stated 260° reflex angle total 350°, not 360°. Preserve both givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Point names, arms, square, reflex arc and 260° are student-visible; the decision and justification are answer-only.

answer.short: No. Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$90^\circ+260^\circ=350^\circ$$
No. Angles completing a turn at a point must sum to $360^\circ$, and $350^\circ\ne360^\circ$.

spec.description: Two arms extend upward-right, one steep and one shallow. The smaller opening contains 50°. An undirected reflex arc wraps left and below the vertex, with 310° at lower left.
spec.mathematics: The minor and reflex angles total 360°. The reflex arc follows the complementary sector, not the small opening.
spec.answerVisibility: Both printed givens and the reflex arc are student-visible. The supplied Yes response is answer-only.

answer.short: Yes. Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$50^\circ+310^\circ=360^\circ$$
Yes. These angles complete a turn at a point.

spec.description: Two straight lines both rise rightward, one steep and one shallow. The acute upper-right and lower-left opposite sectors each contain 35°. Four plain endpoints, without arcs.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled sectors are vertically opposite and both equal 35°.
spec.answerVisibility: Both 35° labels and the complete intersecting lines are student-visible; the response is answer-only.

answer.short: Yes. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
answer.worked: Yes. The labelled angles are vertically opposite and both are $35^\circ$.

spec.description: Two continuous straight lines form a shallow X. The left sector contains 42° and its vertically opposite right sector contains 138°. No arcs or special line marks.
spec.mathematics: 42° and 138° are opposite, not adjacent. Their inequality is the intentional defect; their sum of 180° does not establish correctness.
spec.answerVisibility: Both inconsistent angle givens remain student-visible. The supplied No response is answer-only.

answer.short: No. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
answer.worked: No. The labelled angles are vertically opposite, but $42^\circ\ne138^\circ$.

spec.description: A right-hand vertex has arms extending upper-left and lower-left. The left-opening minor sector contains 80°. An undirected reflex arc wraps around the right and carries 250° to its right. Preserve the source's schematic opening.
spec.mathematics: 80° + 250° = 330°, not 360°. Drawn slopes do not override the printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The minor label, reflex label, arc and both arms are student-visible; the response is answer-only.

answer.short: No. Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$80^\circ+250^\circ=330^\circ$$
No. Angles completing a turn at a point must sum to $360^\circ$, and $330^\circ\ne360^\circ$.

spec.description: A, D and B lie on one straight line rising rightward. DC descends slightly left. D is above-left of the junction. The DA–DC sector contains 49°; the adjacent DC–DB sector contains 141°. All outer endpoints are named and plain.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled adjacent angles on straight line ADB total 190°, not 180°. Preserve the inconsistency.
spec.answerVisibility: All four point labels and both angle givens are student-visible. The decision and justification are answer-only.

answer.short: No. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$49^\circ+141^\circ=190^\circ$$
No. Adjacent angles on straight line $ADB$ must sum to $180^\circ$, and $190^\circ\ne180^\circ$.

spec.description: A straight line rises from lower-left to upper-right. A third arm descends slightly left from its junction. The lower-left small sector contains 40°, and the adjacent larger sector contains 140°. No point labels or angle marks.
spec.mathematics: The adjacent angles total 180°, consistently with the straight line.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete line, descending arm and both angle givens are student-visible; the response is answer-only.

answer.short: Yes. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$40^\circ+140^\circ=180^\circ$$
Yes. These adjacent angles form a straight angle.

spec.description: Straight line ACB descends rightward. CD extends left and slightly down; CE extends down and slightly right. Sectors on the same side of ACB occur CA–CD, CD–CE, CE–CB, containing 43°, a right-angle square and 37° respectively. C is above-right of the junction.
spec.mathematics: 43° + 90° + 37° = 170°, not 180°. Retain straight-line topology, the right-angle marker and both numerical labels.
spec.answerVisibility: All five point labels, four arms, the square and both numerical givens are student-visible. The response is answer-only.

answer.short: No. Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$43^\circ+90^\circ+37^\circ=170^\circ$$
No. Adjacent angles on straight line $ACB$ must sum to $180^\circ$, and $170^\circ\ne180^\circ$.
